steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Proscenium arch: audience on one side, framed stage — creates a 'fourth wall', common in traditional theatres. | Key Fact: Thrust stage: audience on three sides — intimate, breaks fourth wall, used in Shakespeare's Globe. | Key Fact: In-the-round: audience on all sides — most intimate, actors must keep moving to avoid backs to audience. | Key Fact: Traverse: audience on two opposite sides — creates a catwalk/battle effect, highly dynamic.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Name three stage types and explain how each affects the audience-performer relationship. | A director wants to create an intimate, immersive experience. Which stage type would you recommend and why? | Compare the advantages and disadvantages of performing in-the-round versus a proscenium arch stage.
